correctness.rationale: The actual result, verified against all eight original blob IDs, is the exact scalar zero-count law on H×H for all α>-1, 0≤p<q, d=q−p≥2 and c≠0, not a fixed-w slice claim. The independent Fourier–Laplace derivation gives Kα=2^α(α+1)/π[-i(z−conj(w))]^(-h), h=α+2, and mixed derivative identity ∂z^r∂conj(w)^s K/K=(-1)^r(h)_{r+s}t^{r+s}. The four derivative pairings reduce exactly to Q(t)=1+A[(-1)^dc+conj(c)]t^d+(-1)^d B|c|²t^(2d). Strict gamma midpoint log convexity yields B/A²=Γ(h+2p)Γ(h+2q)/Γ(h+p+q)²>1; this makes the two u=t^d roots simple and nonzero. Even d yields a nonreal conjugate u-pair and exactly d lower-half-plane t-roots. For odd d, the common imaginary sign of u gives respectively d+1 lower roots if Im c>0, d-1 if Im c<0, and d-1 plus precisely two real boundary t-roots if Im c=0. Every lower t is attained by z=a/2+ib/2,w=−a/2+ib/2 for 1/t=a+ib,b>0. d≥2 guarantees N≥2; no corner d=1 or c=0 is inadvertently asserted. Independent quadrature and symbolic identities verify representative normalization/signs; the infinite-domain proof is analytic.
residual_risks: Finite root/integral checks do not cover a continuum of real weights or unbounded jet orders; those rely on strict gamma convexity and angular proof.
Unnormalized y^α dxdy and the precise coefficient orientation are essential. Counting zero scalar fibres is not counting zeros of a fixed w slice.

value.rationale: A canonical differential-functional Bergman Gram kernel poses a natural Lu Qi-Keng-type problem. Here a complete exact structural classification solves every separated two-order support with gap d≥2, all starting orders and all real power weights α>-1, determines the precise parity/complex-phase bifurcation, simplicity, and weight/order invariance, and proves unavoidable off-diagonal zeros. The result yields a usable invariant for infinitely many natural kernels and distinguishes them from pure-jet and adjacent-order zero-free cases; it is not an arbitrary isolated small-parameter slice or a numerical table. The generic differential-sequence series was known and is credited, but its nonadjacent weighted zero location is a separate, motivated calculation; no general multijet solution is claimed.
residual_risks: No general classification for three or more derivative supports or arbitrary weights/domains.
If a previously published all-weight sparse-jet phase theorem is discovered, originality/value must be revisited rather than treating a new certificate as proof.

scientific_limitations: Scalar t-values attained from some (z,w)∈H×H, not a count on a fixed-w slice.
